news.title: Israel-Iran war : Iran president says U.S. naval blockade 'doomed to fail’
news.text: Iran’s president has condemned the ongoing U.S. naval blockade, calling it “doomed to fail” amid rising tensions in the conflict involving Iran, United States, and Israel. The blockade, aimed at restricting Iran’s oil exports, has intensified economic pressure and led to shortages within the country. Despite reports of a fragile ceasefire, the situation on the ground remains highly unstable with continued military and political strain. International observers have raised concerns over the growing humanitarian impact, including civilian hardships and internal crackdowns. Overall, the conflict shows no clear path to resolution, with tensions continuing to escalate.

news.title: 'On our own terms': Rajnath Singh's remark on Operation Sindoor
news.text: Rajnath Singh stated that Operation Sindoor was carried out “on our own terms,” emphasizing India’s independent approach to national security. He highlighted that such operations reflect the country’s growing confidence and capability in defense matters. The remark underscores India’s commitment to safeguarding its interests without external influence. It also sends a strong message about strategic autonomy and preparedness. The statement comes amid heightened focus on military readiness and regional security dynamics. It reinforces the government’s stance on decisive action when required. Overall, it projects strength, sovereignty, and self-reliance in defense policy.

news.title: Air India, IndiGo send SOS to government
news.text: Indian airlines have raised concerns over rising operational pressure due to tensions in West Asia. Surging crude oil prices have increased aviation fuel costs, a major expense for carriers. Airspace restrictions are forcing longer flight routes, especially on international sectors. This leads to higher fuel burn, longer travel times, and increased operational costs. With thin profit margins and currency pressures, airlines are struggling to absorb the impact. They have approached the government seeking urgent support to maintain operations and avoid disruptions.

news.title: Japan Airlines trials humanoid robots as ground handlers
news.text: Japan Airlines has begun trials using humanoid robots as ground handlers to support airport operations. These robots are being tested for tasks like baggage handling and assisting staff on the tarmac. The initiative aims to address labor shortages and improve efficiency in airport services. By integrating robotics, the airline hopes to reduce workload on human staff and enhance safety. If successful, this move could mark a significant step toward automation in the aviation industry

news.title: Tamil Nadu government cannot restrict maternity leave to just 12 weeks for third pregnancy: Madras High Court
news.text: The Madras High Court has ruled that the Government of Tamil Nadu cannot restrict maternity leave to just 12 weeks for a third pregnancy. The court held that such a limitation is not justified and undermines women’s rights and welfare. It emphasized that maternity benefits should be provided in a fair and non-discriminatory manner. The judgment reinforces protections for working women and promotes equitable treatment in employment policies.

news.title: Reschedule work hours, provide drinking water to workers: Centre’s advisory to States on heat wave
news.text: The Ministry of Labour and Employment has advised States to protect workers during the ongoing heatwave. It recommends rescheduling work hours to cooler times, especially for outdoor labourers.Employers must provide safe drinking water, shaded rest areas, and regular breaks. Basic health support like first-aid kits and ORS should be available to prevent heat-related illnesses

news.title: Artemis II Moonship Returns After Key Milestone
news.text: The spacecraft for Artemis II has returned to its launch site after a major test phase. Led by NASA, the mission is a key step toward sending astronauts around the Moon. Engineers will now inspect and prepare the vehicle for upcoming crewed operations. This marks steady progress in plans to advance human space exploration

news.title: She fought her way past security guards. Now she’s Tamil Nadu’s first transgender umpire
news.text: : K. Prithika Yashini became Tamil Nadu’s first transgender cricket umpire after overcoming discrimination. She was once stopped by security guards but continued pursuing her passion for cricket. Through determination, she completed training and earned official certification. Her journey is a strong example of resilience and inclusion in sports.

news.title: IBM launches AI platform Bob to regulate SDLC costs
news.text: IBM has introduced an AI platform called Bob to improve software development by balancing speed with governance and security. It helps manage challenges like technical debt, legacy systems, and fragmented workflows by using modular AI agents across the entire SDLC. The platform can analyze, refactor, and modernize systems faster while maintaining compliance through built-in guardrails and human oversight. It also optimizes performance using multiple AI models and ensures transparency with full traceability of actions. Overall, Bob significantly boosts developer productivity and reduces development time while maintaining enterprise-level control and reliability.

didYouKnow.title: AI Code Explosion
didYouKnow.content: Over 40% of code written in 2026 is now generated by AI tools, drastically changing how software is built and tested.

didYouKnow.title: Digital Twins
didYouKnow.content: Entire cities are now being replicated as digital twins using AI, allowing governments to simulate disasters and traffic before they happen in real life.

didYouKnow.title: Brain-Computer Interface
didYouKnow.content: Scientists have successfully enabled humans to type using only their thoughts, achieving speeds close to smartphone typing.

didYouKnow.title: Quantum Threat
didYouKnow.content: Future quantum computers could break most current encryption methods, forcing the world to redesign internet security from scratch.

didYouKnow.title: AI Hallucination
didYouKnow.content: AI models can confidently generate completely false information, known as hallucinations, making human validation more critical than ever.
